items.text: Inspector action model fully defined per node type per lens. 6 node types × 3 lenses yields a sparse matrix (not every node appears in every lens). Key actions: Capture → Classify/Create item (Topology only). BacklogItem → Edit/Queue/Workshop (Topology), Queue/View history/Follow-up (Flow). Initiative → Edit/Add-remove items (Topology). Scenario → View files/Edit (Topology), Start/Stop/Restart/Logs (Operations). ExecutionRecord → Prompt trace/Follow-up/Retry/Review (Flow), Stop/Logs (Operations). Run → Stop/View in agent-manager (Operations only). Inspector renders as desktop popover (anchored to node, viewport-clamped) or mobile bottom sheet.

Migration route mapping complete. Current 7 routes map to: / → Graph workspace (Topology lens default), /backlog → sidebar + graph, /backlog/:kind/:name → preserved as deep link that auto-selects node + opens inspector, /scenarios/:name → preserved similarly, /execution → Flow lens, /prompts → reference drawer (gear menu), /settings → settings modal (gear icon). Agent-manager deep links (navigate to /backlog/:kind/:name) continue to work unchanged. URL strategy: workspace at / with ?lens= query param.

Performance estimates based on store analysis: Topology lens ~85-370 nodes, Flow ~100-400, Operations ~11-60. Anti-chaos rules: initiative clustering (collapsed by default with rollup), status filters per lens, ~50 unclustered node cap with overflow pseudo-node, 300-edge threshold for lightweight edges, 500-edge warning to narrow filters, MiniMap visible between 20-120 nodes. Operations polling: 5s for active runs, 30s for scenario status.

Execute-item decomposition formalized as 6 items: (1) Graph Data Foundation — /api/v1/graph endpoint [M effort, P1], (2) Graph Workspace Shell — sidebar+canvas+inspector frame [L effort, P1], (3) Topology + Scenario Impact Views [L effort, P1, depends on 1+2], (4) Flow + Operations Views [L effort, P2, depends on 1+2], (5) Remove Legacy Tabbed Surfaces [M effort, P3, depends on 3+4], (6) Mobile Graph Optimization [M effort, P2, depends on 2]. Critical path: items 1+2 (parallel) → 3 → 5.

This research appears ready for conclusion. All 5 readiness dimensions are at 2+. The conclusion now covers all 6 spec deliverables: graph workspace architecture, canonical node/edge contract, lens definitions, inspector action model, rollout/cleanup plan, and execute-item decomposition. The remaining testability gap (score 2 vs 3) is inherent — full verification requires building the graph and testing with real data, which is the job of the execute items.

items.context: The current mobile UI uses a bottom nav bar with immersive mode for detail routes. A graph workspace needs a fundamentally different mobile approach. Three options trade off between graph fidelity and usability on small screens.

options.label: Adaptive layout: full graph canvas with simplified nodes, bottom sheet inspector
options.rationale: Preserve the graph on mobile with touch optimizations (pinch/zoom, 44px hit targets, long-press context). Hamburger menu for sidebar. Reduced node detail (icon + title only). ~30 node mobile cap. This keeps the graph-first paradigm consistent across devices but may feel cramped on phones.

options.label: List-first mobile: sidebar feed as primary, graph as optional secondary view
options.rationale: Mobile defaults to the activity feed (sidebar content) as a scrollable list. Graph is accessible via a toggle but not the default. Simpler mobile UX, works well for quick status checks. Risk: mobile users never discover the graph.

items.topic: URL and routing strategy for deep link preservation
items.context: Agent-manager integration creates deep links to /backlog/:kind/:name via the agent-run dropdown. The graph workspace replaces page-based navigation with graph node selection. We need a URL strategy that preserves these entry points.

options.label: Preserve current paths as deep-link entry points, workspace at / with ?lens= param
options.rationale: Keep /backlog/:kind/:name and /scenarios/:name as valid URLs that resolve to the graph workspace with the matching node auto-selected and inspector opened. Lens defaults to Topology for backlog/scenario links. Workspace root is / with ?lens=topology|flow|operations. No old routes break. Agent-manager needs zero changes.

options.label: New URL scheme: /graph?lens=X&select=kind/name, redirect old paths
options.rationale: All graph state lives under /graph with query params. Old /backlog/:kind/:name paths 301-redirect to /graph?lens=topology&select=:kind/:name. Cleaner URL model but requires redirect handling and agent-manager clients to eventually update.

items.context: The Operations lens shows live scenario status and agent run state. This requires periodic data refresh. The agent-manager proxy already supports GET /api/v1/agent-manager/runs/{runID} and GET /api/v1/agent-manager/status. The question is how to refresh efficiently.

options.label: Polling: 5s for active runs, 30s for scenario status, pause when lens not active
options.rationale: Simple and proven. Two polling intervals match the data freshness needs (runs change fast, scenarios change slowly). Pause polling when user switches to Topology or Flow lens to reduce server load. Resume on lens switch. Existing AgentRunsStore already uses a polling pattern.

options.label: Server-Sent Events (SSE) for push-based updates
options.rationale: Backend pushes status changes via SSE stream. Lower latency, no wasted polls. But requires new SSE infrastructure in the API, connection management, reconnection logic, and proxy considerations. Higher implementation cost for v1.

plan_updates: Major conclusion update: added 4 new findings (Finding 6: inspector action model per node/lens, Finding 7: migration route mapping with URL strategy, Finding 8: performance estimates and anti-chaos guardrails, Finding 9: mobile interaction model). Filled the Actions section with 6 concrete execute-item specifications including kinds, titles, descriptions, priorities, efforts, and dependencies. Updated Summary to reflect full contract scope. All spec deliverables now covered.
